gĕōmē^tres , ae (also gĕōmē^tra , Aur. Vict. Ep. 14, 2;
I. “and gĕŏmetra, ae,” Sid. Ep. 4, 11 : “ge[dibreve]omētrēs, trisyl.,” Juv. 3, 76 ), m., = γεωμέτρης, a geometer, geometrician: “quomodo geometres cernere ea potest quae aut nulla sunt aut internosci a falsis non possunt?” Cic. Ac. 2, 7, 22 : “geometres,” Quint. 1, 10, 6 ; Juv. 3, 76.—Dat. geometrae, Quint. 1, 12, 6.—Acc. geometren, id. 1, 10, 4.— Plur.: “geometrae,” Cic. Off. 3, 7, 33 ; id. Fat. 8, 15; Quint. 12, 11, 20; Fragm. Jur. Rom. Vatic. 150 Huschke.—Dat. geometris, id. 1, 10, 18.—Acc. geometras, id. 5, 10, 7.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
